description: Extreme-difficulty benchmark suite — schema-compatible with benchmark_quality.py. Designed to break 100% pass rates on capable 27B local models. Draws from HumanEval hard (is_nested, word_ladder, N-Queens, min_window), LeetCode Hard (LIS, expr evaluator, itinerary, max_product, merge_intervals, combo_count), competition math (AIME-style modular arithmetic, Bayesian probability, infinite series), 10-tool agentic disambiguation (post_webhook, translate_text), and deep MCP schema reasoning (nested date_range, idempotency_key, compress vs resize).

context_window_notes.note: MCP system prompts are ~400-500 tokens; agentic ~300 tokens
context_window_notes.thinking_mode: max_tokens values are sized for --think mode (includes thinking token budget). Without --think the model will be faster and still have ample token headroom.

tests.name: is_nested_brackets
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `is_nested(string)` that accepts a string of square brackets and returns True if and only if there exists at least one bracket that is nested inside another pair of brackets. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: word_ladder_bfs
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `word_ladder(begin_word, end_word, word_list)` that returns the length of the shortest transformation sequence from begin_word to end_word, where each step changes exactly one letter and every word must be in word_list. The length is the total number of words in the sequence (including begin and end). Return 0 if no sequence exists. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: n_queens_count
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `n_queens(n)` that returns the total number of distinct solutions to the N-Queens problem on an n×n board. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: minimum_window_substring
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `min_window(s, t)` that returns the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included. Return empty string if no such window exists. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: longest_increasing_subsequence
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `lis(nums)` that returns the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Use an O(n log n) algorithm. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: expression_evaluator
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `evaluate(s)` that evaluates a string arithmetic expression containing non-negative integers, +, -, *, / operators and parentheses. Integer division truncates toward zero. Spaces may appear anywhere. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: reconstruct_itinerary
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `find_itinerary(tickets)` where tickets is a list of [from, to] string pairs. Reconstruct the itinerary starting from 'JFK' using all tickets exactly once. Return the itinerary with smallest lexicographic order when multiple solutions exist. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: max_product_subarray
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `max_product(nums)` that returns the maximum product of a contiguous non-empty subarray of nums. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: count_unordered_combinations
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `count_combinations(candidates, target)` that counts the number of distinct combinations (ORDER DOES NOT MATTER) of numbers from candidates that sum to target. Each number may be used unlimited times. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: merge_overlapping_intervals
tests.prompt: Write a Python function `merge(intervals)` that merges all overlapping intervals. Input is a list of [start, end] pairs. Return a sorted list of merged intervals. Output only the function definition.

tests.name: combinatorics_committee
tests.prompt: A club has 10 members. How many different 2-person committees can be formed? Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: digit_sum_enumeration
tests.prompt: How many three-digit positive integers (from 100 to 999 inclusive) have digits that sum to exactly 20? Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: geometric_distribution_expected_value
tests.prompt: You roll a fair six-sided die repeatedly until you get a 6. What is the expected number of rolls required? Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: tower_exponent_mod_100
tests.prompt: What are the last two digits of 7 raised to the power (7 raised to the power 7)? In other words, compute 7^(7^7) mod 100. Give only the final two-digit integer answer.

tests.name: right_triangle_inradius_area
tests.prompt: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 26 and an inradius of 5. What is the area of the triangle? Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: bayesian_factory_defect
tests.prompt: A company has two factories. Factory 1 produces 60% of items with a 2% defect rate. Factory 2 produces 40% of items with a 5% defect rate. Given that a randomly selected item is defective, what is the probability (as a decimal) that it came from Factory 2? Round to 3 decimal places. Give only the numeric answer.

tests.name: series_sum_k_over_2k
tests.prompt: Compute the exact value of the infinite series: S = 1/2 + 2/4 + 3/8 + 4/16 + ... = sum from k=1 to infinity of k divided by 2^k. Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: divisor_count_prime_factorization
tests.prompt: How many positive divisors does the number 2^3 × 3^2 × 5 × 7^2 have? Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: geometric_sequence_common_ratio
tests.prompt: A geometric sequence has first term 2. The sum of its first 5 terms is 62. What is the common ratio? Give only the final integer answer.

tests.name: max_rectangle_in_circle
tests.prompt: What is the maximum area of a rectangle that can be inscribed in a circle of radius 5? Give only the final integer answer.
